newsitem.title: LIBYA: OAU summit on Central Africa on March 26.
newsitem.headline: OAU summit on Central Africa on March 26.

text.p: African states will hold a summit on March 26 at Lome, Togo on the situation in the Great Lakes region of Central Africa with a special focus on eastern Zaire, the Organisation of African Unity said on Friday.

OAU Secretary General Salim Ahmed Salim told reporters at the end of an OAU foreign ministers' meeting that the summit was being put off from March 18-19 to 26 to ensure a better attendance of heads of state.

Salim said: "We are inviting all the neighbouring countries and also the countries involved in finding a solution to the crisis, such as the president of South Africa and Kenya and the presidents of the African countries who are members of the U.N. Security Council -- Guinea Bissau, Egypt.
"We will also invite Libya, as current chairman of the (OAU) council of ministers session."
He added: "Other countries who would like to attend will be able to do so as observers."
Earlier, African foreign ministers at the meeting in Tripoli invited Zaire to attend the summit.
"All the states in the Central Africa region were invited to Togo summit," Ibrahim Daggash, a spokesman for the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) told reporters. He did not elaborate.
Zairean Foreign Minister Kamanda Wa Kamanda said: "The OAU decision means that Zaire is invited to the Togo meeting."

The rebels have overrun a 1,000 km (600-mile) stretch of Zaire since they took up arms in October against ailing President Sese Seko Mobutu, a veteran leader they call a despot and have vowed to topple. Rebels said they had taken one side of the commercial and transport hub of Kindu on Friday.
The summit was called at the request of Togo, Benin and Nigeria.
